questions.question:
D3 — Which implementation approach for the processPayment() tests?
Project: Payment Processing — Test Coverage (main)
ELI10: The plan calls for 2 unit tests. The question is how precise those tests should be. A loose test says “assert a receipt came back”; a tight test says “assert receipt.amount == 50, receipt.charge_id == mock_id, and Stripe was called exactly once.” Tight tests catch more regressions but take slightly more time to write.
Stakes if we pick wrong: Loose assertions let partial regressions ship undetected — the payment goes through but the receipt is wrong. Missing call-count assertions mean the retry path could silently stop retrying and the test would still pass.
Recommendation: B because the mock call history and virtual sleeper already exist to assert exact behavior — not using them wastes the infrastructure and leaves the retry proof hollow.
Completeness: A=5/10, B=7/10, C=9/10
<gstack-qid:plan-ceo-review-impl-approach>

options.label: A) Minimal as Described
options.description: Add exactly 2 tests per the plan: happy path + 502. Basic assertions only (“correct receipt generated”, “fails clean”). Smallest diff. Effort: human ~1 hr / CC ~5 min. Completeness: 5/10.

options.label: B) 2 Tests + Explicit Assertions (Recommended)
options.description: Same 2 tests but with concrete assertions: receipt field values, Stripe call count = 2, virtual sleeper backoff invocation recorded. Proves retry mechanism actually fired. Effort: human ~1.5 hr / CC ~8 min. Completeness: 7/10.

options.label: C) Coverage Sweep
options.description: 2 primary tests + nil/empty input cases + explicit out-of-scope comment while already in the file. Closes more gaps in one PR. Effort: human ~3 hr / CC ~15 min. Completeness: 9/10.
